P1.evidence: The weakest open in the batch. After rapport about football and the Netherlands, the rep went straight in with 'I would say, yeah, let's just dive into it. So just take me through it. Like, what can we potentially help you out with?' There is no frame at all — no statement of where we're going, no 'what's in the way', no 'what you need', and no disqualification clause, all of which he delivered on his other calls. Consequently no frame agreement was sought either. Only the open question ran.

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight all asked directly at 00:05:37. Nutrition was covered thoroughly and well — current intake, meal prep, protein powder, creatine, a specific protein-gram estimate, and the nature of his cheat meals, which produced the useful insight that his issue is quantity rather than quality. Occupation surfaced as photographer with a noon start, but the rep never asked whether the work is sedentary, which matters given the prospect attributes his back pain to 'sitting too long'. Health conditions were never asked. Injuries were asked once — 'Any aches, pains that sometimes come up for you?' — which surfaced intermittent lower back pain, and the prospect later volunteered that he pulled his back within the last couple of years; neither was followed up for duration, severity or cause. Training frequency was never pinned to a number of days. Sleep and daily energy were both never raised.

P3.evidence: Well run. The focus question and the mobility-strength-energy fork both ran, and the specific-limitation question produced concrete answers — tight hips, four or five pull-ups. The bridge ran cleanly: 'Is there anything besides just a physical aspect that's sort of driving you for wanting to do something with this now?' — which surfaced the deepest material in the call, wanting to record his peak lifetime strength before decline and to be in shape for children in the next couple of years. The impact question was asked twice, patiently, through the prospect's 'What do you mean?', and eventually landed on 'It would just mean joy. I'd be happier, I'd be healthier.' The reflect-back ran with a confirmation check: 'it sounds like your actual why mainly comes from potentially kids in the future, but also wanting to maximize your life overall, is that correct?' Marked down only because 'who else does that impact?' was never asked — the wife, family and career were volunteered — and the drive into legacy stopped as soon as the prospect offered it rather than being deepened.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase in the batch so far and genuinely good coaching. History was drawn out in full — high school sports, training for the wedding, and the prospect's own damning summary: 'I get to a place that I'm happy with, and then I decline, and then I hate myself... it's just a sick cycle.' The rep then asked the root-cause question directly ('Why do you think that you sort of fall off after those two, three months?') and, crucially, challenged the answer instead of accepting it: told 'just general laziness' and then 'maturity', he pushed back with 'I'm still speaking to people who sometimes 40, 50, sixty-year-olds who still have that laziness aspect... is there something that made you be more mature?' — which produced the real answer about career, kids and larger life events. He also ran the blocker question well: 'would there be anything else besides basically that laziness aspect that would stop you from committing?' Marked down because the gap was never named against the scripted list, and the 'information isn't the problem' challenge only appeared much later as an objection rebuttal rather than here.

P5.evidence: Attempted but shallow. The projection question was asked without a horizon — 'what would that look like if you just sort of keep going up in the same way that you've been going?' — and the prospect deflected it into a shopping answer, 'I'll probably be looking for another solution', which the rep accepted rather than redirecting. No two-year frame was ever set. The settle question ran and got a clean 'No, no', but the prospect immediately softened it with 'I mean, I'm not unhappy', and that softening was never challenged. 'Why not?' was never asked and there was no line-in-the-sand question. For a prospect whose entire presenting problem is a decades-long cycle of falling off, the cost of continuing that cycle was never made concrete.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran twice, once after the training block and once after the full presentation: 'do you feel like you're then also going to be able to stick to it and maximize your life and get more strength?' — answered 'Yeah, I do. I just need a little bit of guidance.' But the all-in isolation question was never asked in any form, and that omission decided the call: had 'is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' been put before the number, the need to consult his wife would have surfaced before price rather than three minutes after it. The yes obtained was also a soft one, qualified in the same breath with 'I don't need that much guidance', and the rep moved to price without resolving that hedge.

P11.evidence: A price was given and next steps were raised, so the phase applies, but no attempt was made to collect. The rep said 'Next steps is that we would get you started with that' and then answered logistics questions until the prospect deferred; the card was never asked for. Onboarding with Trevor and the signed agreement do not exist for the lower-tier community product, so those two steps are marked not applicable rather than missed. The rep did explain the Skool platform and offered to send a link, which is a partial on the final step, but he accepted 'just send it to my email' without a second attempt to close.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered verbatim by 'I'm gonna have to think about it.' The rep ran one move well and stopped. He challenged the DIY alternative against the prospect's own history — 'Isn't that something you've been trying to do for the last however long?' — and got the concession 'Yeah, absolutely'. He also tested the value and got 'it's certainly worth $200 a month', which is effectively the scripted belief check. But none of the rest ran: no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?', and no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?'. Having just extracted an admission that the prospect has failed at self-programming for years, the rep had the strongest possible setup for those moves and did not use it.

Triggered by 'I'm going to go talk to my wife about it.' Two scripted moves ran in substance: whether she supports his decisions ('Do you feel like your wife does support you in whatever decisions you make when it comes to physical health?' — 'Yeah, of course') and background on whether she knows about his efforts. The core moves were all missed: no 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal?', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up?', no 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself?', no 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house', and no deposit-with-refund fallback. Instead the rep asked an unscripted question — 'And what if she says no?' — which the prospect rejected outright with 'This isn't a marriage therapy class.' The rep read the room and disengaged, which was the right call at that point, but the play was effectively over.

A light trigger rather than a full one, but present in substance: 'it's certainly worth $200 a month. But there's other aspects of, you know, finances and things that go down.' That is an explicit statement that competing financial commitments are in play, and nothing ran against it — no isolation, no open-conversation permission, and none of the financial picture. Given that the prospect had already anchored his budget at $100-150 a month, this was the moment to establish whether $200 was genuinely affordable or whether the pivot to a cheaper product had simply moved the same objection down a tier.

Script gap. The prospect asked directly what the one-to-one programme costs and what it entails, twice, and stated a budget anchor before any number was presented. The playbook has no guidance for handling a stated budget that sits far below the offer — no disqualification path, no reframe, and no instruction on whether a lower-priced product may be presented instead. In the absence of one the rep gave an imprecise answer about the flagship price and moved to a different product. That is a process gap with real commercial consequences and is recorded in the flags.

notes: Past Attempts was the best-run phase in the batch — he drew out the cycle, refused to accept 'laziness' and 'maturity' as answers, and pushed until the real driver appeared. Goals was strong too. Everything around the money was weak: no frame at the open, no cost of inaction, no all-in isolation before price, and no attempt to collect at the end. The decisive error came earlier, when he asked for the prospect's budget before presenting anything and then let that anchor determine which product got presented, giving an inaccurate figure for the flagship along the way. Coach on presenting the actual offer before conceding to a stated budget, and on isolating before price so a spouse objection cannot arrive after the number.
